Mention any THREE points of significance of mitosis in plants.
Mitosis increases cell number during root and shoot growth, replaces damaged cells during repair, and allows vegetative reproduction with genetically similar offspring.
One mark each for three distinct functions, such as growth, repair and vegetative reproduction.
2a

How is the composition of blood maintained by the following functions of nephron in the human kidney?

• Secretion (1 mark)
• Reabsorption (1 mark)
Secretion moves selected wastes or excess ions from the blood into the tubule. Reabsorption restores useful substances, such as glucose, and regulated amounts of water and salts to the blood.
One mark each for linking secretion and reabsorption to blood composition. Direction of transfer is essential.
2b
Describe any TWO adaptive features of human skin to maintain body temperature during a cold day. (2 marks)
Skin arterioles constrict, reducing blood flow near the surface and reducing heat loss. Sweat glands release less sweat, reducing evaporative cooling.
One mark per described feature tied to heat conservation. Naming a response alone is insufficient.

i. Describe ONE function of each of the five components of reflex action. (5 marks)
ii. Mention any ONE feature of a reflex action that differentiates it from a voluntary action. (1 mark)

i. Receptor detects a stimulus. Sensory neuron carries an impulse to the CNS. Relay neuron conveys it within the CNS. Motor neuron carries the impulse to the effector. Effector produces the response.
ii. A reflex is automatic and does not require a conscious decision.
One mark for each of the five roles and one for a valid distinction from voluntary action.
5b

i. Describe the structural adaptations of the following parts of a wind-pollinated flower.

• Pollen (1 mark)
• Stamen (1 mark)
• Stigma (1 mark)

ii. Mention the importance of each structural adaptation described in part i. (3 marks)
Light, dry pollen is readily carried by air. Exposed anthers on flexible filaments release pollen into moving air. Projecting feathery stigmas have more surface area to intercept airborne pollen.
One mark per structural feature and one per matching advantage, up to six.
6a

Describe in TWO points each of the following causes of genetic variation in a population.

• Mutation (2 marks)
• Gene flow between populations (2 marks)
• Random assortment of homologous chromosomes (2 marks)

Mutation changes DNA and can create new alleles. A heritable mutation can be passed to descendants. Gene flow occurs when individuals or gametes move and reproduce across populations. It introduces alleles or changes allele frequencies in the receiving population. During meiosis I, homologous pairs orient independently. This produces different combinations of parental chromosomes in gametes.
Two points each for mutation, gene flow and random assortment. Link each process to variation.
6b

Describe the effect of open dumping of solid wastes into oceans on the following.

• Aquatic ecosystem (2 marks)
• Economic loss and fisheries management cost (2 marks)
• Public safety (2 marks)

Aquatic ecosystem: debris can entangle animals and be swallowed, causing injury or death. Economic effects: damaged gear and reduced catches lower income, and monitoring and clean-up cost money. Public safety: sharp debris injures swimmers, and contaminated water or seafood can expose people to harmful substances.
Two valid, distinct effects in each category, up to six marks.
